correctness.rationale: The normalized tangential-gradient Gram identity follows from ∇_S(x^TQx)=2(Qx−(x^TQx)x), global Laplace eigenvalue 2d, and explicit degree-two and degree-four absolute Gaussian sphere moments. In harmonic coordinates u∈1⊥ and edge coefficients v, the resulting four-term plus cross Hermitian form is diagonalized by BB^T=(d−2)I+J, giving exactly the four listed sectors and multiplicities. Polynomial evaluations p(alpha_d)<0 and p(L_d)<0 with alpha_d<L_d prove the strict global eigenvalue ordering for every d≥3; regional unique continuation makes all actual eigenvalues strictly between 0 and 1. The two-by-two determinant/trace asymptotic gives κ(G_d)=d/(π−2)+O(1). Packaged independent moment Gram reconstruction passed all degrees d=3,...,10 (243 assertions), and six symbolic factorizations passed. Limits: numerical checks are finite corroborations, not proofs.

value.rationale: The exact observation mask is canonical for incomplete-domain spherical signals; choosing measured tangential gradients rather than values corresponds to derivative-based physical information. The result proves a substantive structural contrast with the already-known scalar orthant operator: two standard (d−1)-dimensional extremal eigenspaces instead of a unique scalar top sector, and exactly linear concentration spectral conditioning d/(π−2)+O(1) instead of a quadratic law. Full all-dimensional spectral classification and sharp asymptotic constant are mathematical statements not obtainable from finite trials alone. No claims about noisy or discrete acquisition are made.
